program: Home-delivered nutrition, wellbeing checks and senior transportation
priceScope: Conditional full annual recipient cost versus limited home-delivered nutrition/connection and net food-resource channel; not complete portfolio EV or verified marginal gift.

what: Meals on Wheels Montgomery County brings meals and friendly wellbeing checks to homebound older residents.
Its separate transportation program provides accessible rides to essential appointments and errands.
Congregate meals and other support help local seniors maintain nutrition and independence.
strengths: Latest original return distinguishes unique home-delivered recipients from meals and transport trips.
Primary randomized evidence supports a connection mechanism against a waiting-list alternative.
Signed food resources and exposure costs are modeled separately from clinical health, with complete original diagnostics.
reservations: Meals, survey satisfaction and independence claims are not causal clinical outcomes.
Service duration is a meal-density proxy, not observed completed dose for each person.
Net grocery savings, household overlap, volunteer costs and next-donation response remain unmeasured.

sections.what: Meals on Wheels Montgomery County brings meals and friendly wellbeing checks to homebound older residents. Its separate transportation program provides accessible rides to essential appointments and errands. Congregate meals and other support help local seniors maintain nutrition and independence.
sections.monitoring: Fresh original FYending September 2025 return: 227,136 home-delivered meals to 1,178 seniors; 19,145 trips to 493 people; 781 congregate dinners. Transport and meal recipients may overlap and are not added. Homepage's 340,000 meals and story's self-reported emotional health/main meal claims use different scope and no controlled counterfactual. Average 192.82 meals per annual unique recipient corresponds to 38.56 five-meal weeks, or .7416 year of weekday exposure. This is not a verified enrollment-duration distribution, daily contact frequency or causal health dose. Request entry/exit, meal uptake, actual unique household/spouse overlap, nutritional risk and loneliness before/after against alternatives, net grocery expenditure, SNAP and family substitution, caregiver resources and access harms.
sections.qualitative: The original More Than a Meal randomized study assigned 626 waiting-list seniors across eight programs to daily delivery, weekly delivery or waiting list; loneliness was lower in meal groups at 15 weeks, with delivery modality important. This supports one combined nutrition/connection clinical stream, not added separate loneliness utility or a local .02 QALY coefficient. The original falls-trial abstract covers 371 people: daily RR .83 (CI .55–1.25), weekly .96 (CI .63–1.45), so no established overall falls reduction is imported. Original HOMEFOOD full PDF studied 106 post-discharge at-risk adults with six-month individualized nutrition, home visits, calls and enriched food/supplements; endpoint EQ-5D difference .102 is not integrated QALYs or the effect of this local weekday meal program. Its endpoint-transfer sensitivity is explicitly hypothetical. Current local eligibility excludes an existing resident caregiver/family member except spouse and an authorized meal-preparation provider, constraining large generic caregiver-labor claims. Household or spouse resource changes are joint-netted; distinct external caregivers cannot be added without their own incidence ledger. Existing SNAP, family meals, delivery options and public nutrition are retained alternatives.
sections.cost: Initial $17.86M per better life is preserved, with 1.753991 clinical QALYs and 1.044375 signed resource equivalents. Applying full exposure burdens alone gives $36.59M; using native meal-density exposure to refine health and net-resource duration gives current $49.68M: health 0.911877, income 0.093974, total 1.005850 equivalent healthy years. Current full annual cost $4,996,818 versus this limited channel is not whole portfolio EV or demonstrated next-dollar impact. The .3 additionality, .4 clinical response and .02 utility remain judgments, not survey or trial coefficients. T and fraction of annual resource gains move from .75/1 to .741596/.741596 using 227,136/(1,178*260); averaging meals cannot establish equal duration or delivery contact, so trial-length 15-week and other finite sensitivities are explicit. Full .001 health harm and $30 one-off access/preparation/time cost apply to all 1,178 individual-consumption proxies, independent of b; benefit union remains 353.4 and resource-success group 176.7. Native seniors are unique people, not verified unique households: spouse and household mapping sensitivity remains. One welfare-equivalent adult allocation per recipient at $20,000 baseline prevents adding all family members. The $600 annual net-food-resource hypothesis means genuinely avoided grocery/care cash after SNAP, alternative family purchases, food replacement and benefit withdrawal—not retail meal price, medical savings or gross subsidy. Only .741596 year's amount is realized and positive overlap .5 removes duplicated nutrition welfare before full $30 cost; unsuccessful recipients retain costs. Medical savings and caregiver/work gains are unknown-neutral zero centrally, with positive and negative hypotheses tested, not assumed survivor salaries. All gains/costs within overlapping recipients use one log. Distinct public/private payer and volunteer losses are localized once and not discounted as positive overlap. Payer/provider incidence remains unknown; recipient-paid meal expense already in C is not charged twice. Transportation, congregate meals, other portfolio channels and paid-caregiver effects remain unknown, not zero. Clinical-null, financial-only, no-benefit with costs, true no-exposure/no-gift, adverse, low/high burden, negative gains, payer incidence and economic-cost scenarios remain finite/testable. A recognized home-delivery program-cost sensitivity uses $2,206,008 against the same meal-only benefits, giving $21.93M per better life. That boundary excludes allocated fundraising, overhead and volunteer resources; it is not full resource cost, whole portfolio EV or a verified marginal donation offer.
sections.funding: Latest original tax period October 2024–September 2025 (form tax label 2024): functional expense $4,626,696 plus netted direct event expense $370,122 gives $4,996,818. FYending 2024 $4,236,946+$526,825=$4,763,771; FYending 2023 $3,752,082+$198,150=$3,950,232. FY2025 home-delivery expense $2,206,008, transport $1,161,088 and congregate $469,223 explain why full cost exceeds this meal-only benefit channel; none is gross-summed again. Current $2,600 care solicitation and 100-day waitlist are not verified marginal price or funded capacity. Volunteers and external care opportunity costs remain unknown; $6.5M full-resource scenario is a judgment, not observed accounting. Fresh original source confirms EIN 23-7310650; official donor route was checked without a transaction. The program-aligned sensitivity quantifies the cost-boundary effect without attributing unknown transportation or congregate benefits to meals.

model.costScope: Whole annual recognized recipient cost versus conditional meal nutrition/check-in and netcash channel; otherprograms and externalcost unknown
model.geographicAttribution: Montgomery County inHouston metro; full1.0 localshare once
model.formula: Exposed=N*unique; benefit union=exposed*b. Clinical=(clinicalN*unique*b*clinicalResponse*q*finite discounted T − exposed*harm/onset discount)*g. Changed=union*success; one joint household log of positive-only overlap net food/medical/work/transfer resources*resourceYears minus full cost; other exposed retains full cost. Distinct payer loss localized once. Price=10*C/(health+signed resources).
model.counterfactual: Family/caregiver meals, SNAP/publicnutrition, grocerydelivery and paidmeal alternatives retained
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Unique recipient and full finance source-grounded; households, causal fraction, local utility and net cash unmeasured. Average meal-density is a duration proxy, not matched dosage. Trial evidence supports mechanisms and bounds, not automatic local coefficients. Other portfolio and current gift EV unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Unique oldermeal recipients, finite nutritional/connection utility and actual cashcosts avoided; notmeals,retailvalue or self-reportedcausality
